anhui-agricultural-university: Anhui Agricultural University, often shortened to AHAU, is a public university based in Hefei, the capital of Anhui. Its roots go back to 1928, and today it serves roughly 20,904 students. Backing comes from the provincial government alongside two national bodies for agriculture and forestry, which gives the campus a clear focus on the land and its sciences.
anhui-medical-university: Anhui Medical University opened in 1926 and is a public medical university in Hefei, Anhui. About 18,700 students study here, preparing for careers in health and medicine. Support comes from the provincial government, the Education Ministry and the National Health Commission together, so it is a solid option if you hope to train in medicine in China.
anhui-normal-university: Anhui Normal University is a public institution of higher learning in Wuhu, a city in Anhui Province. It opened its doors in 1928, which makes it one of the region's long-standing schools. As a normal university, its tradition lies in preparing teachers, so it may appeal to you if education is the career you have in mind.
anhui-university: Anhui University, known as AHU, sits in Hefei, the capital of Anhui, and has roots going back to 1928. It is a provincial public university with around 49000 students, supported by the provincial government, the Education Ministry and SASTIND. It also takes part in Project 211 as well as the Double First-Class Construction, two national programmes for leading universities.
anshan-normal-university: Anshan Normal University can be found in Anshan, a city of Liaoning province, and answers to the provincial government. It started out in 1958 as a centre training teachers, paused during the Cultural Revolution, and reopened in 1978. The campus spreads over 731,600 square meters, and its teaching staff numbers 1207, from professors to postgraduate teachers.
beihang-university: Beihang University is a public research university in the Haidian district of Beijing, founded in 1952. It has about 12,523 students and is overseen by the industry and information technology ministry. It also joins Project 211 and Project 985, plus the Double First-Class Construction, three national initiatives that mark it as a leading Chinese institution.
beihua-university: Beihua University lies in Jilin City, in China's Jilin province, and is a public school run under the Jilin Provincial Government. Its history goes all the way back to 1906, so it carries more than a century of tradition. If you are looking at northeastern China for your studies, this is a well-established local choice to explore.
beijing-film-academy: Beijing Film Academy, or BFA, is a public college in Beijing devoted to the film arts, founded in 1950. It belongs to the city, with funding shared between the municipal government, the national broadcasting regulator and the Education Ministry. It is a natural place to look if you dream of working in cinema.
beijing-foreign-studies-university: Beijing Foreign Studies University, known as BFSU, is a public national university in the Haidian district of Beijing. It has been running since 1941 and reports to the Education Ministry. Being part of the Double First-Class Construction, along with Project 211 shows it is well recognised for languages and international studies within the Chinese system.
beijing-forestry-university: Beijing Forestry University, or BFU, is a public university in Beijing, established in 1952. It is overseen by the Education Ministry, with extra support from the national forestry and grassland authority and the Beijing government. Thanks to its place in Project 211, plus the Double First-Class Construction, it is a strong choice if forests and the environment interest you.
beijing-institute-of-technology: Beijing Institute of Technology, called BIT, can be found in Haidian, Beijing. Its origins lie in 1940, when it opened in Shaanxi under the name Yan'an Natural Science Academy, and has been run by the MIIT since 2008. It joins Project 211, Project 985 and also the Double First-Class Construction, making it a prominent technical university.
beijing-international-studies-university: Beijing International Studies University, or BISU, specialises in foreign languages and stands in the Chaoyang district of Beijing. It is also known as the Beijing Second College of Foreign Languages. This public college belongs to the city and is funded jointly by the Beijing government and the culture and tourism ministry, which suits language learners.
beijing-jiaotong-university: Beijing Jiaotong University, or BJTU, has roots in 1896 and stands in Haidian, Beijing. About 14,620 students study here. Earlier it was called Northern Jiaotong University, and the name points to its transport heritage. Several ministries and a railway group help fund it, and it takes part in Project 211 and the national Double First-Class Construction drive.
beijing-language-and-culture-university: Beijing Language and Culture University, or BLCU, is a public linguistics university in Haidian, Beijing, set up in 1962 under the Ministry of Education. Its central purpose is teaching Chinese language and culture to students from abroad, and it is the only international university of its kind named after language, which makes it a natural home for newcomers.
beijing-normal-university: Beijing Normal University, or BNU, has stood in Haidian, Beijing since 1902. It has a strong name for training teachers, education science and basic learning across arts and sciences. The Education Ministry and the Beijing government support it, and it belongs to Project 211, Project 985 and also the Double First-Class Construction.
beijing-sport-university: Beijing Sport University, or BSU, is a public university in Beijing dedicated to sport, founded in 1953. Around 14,000 students study here. It reports to China's national sports administration and takes part in the 211 Project and the Double First-Class Construction, so it is a great fit for aspiring athletes and coaches.
beijing-technology-and-business-universi: Beijing Technology and Business University, called BTBU, belongs to the city of Beijing and began in 1950. It has roughly 12,000 students. It came together from a merger of a light industry school, a business school and an administration school linked to the Ministry of Machinery Industry, giving it a practical mix of subjects.
beijing-university-of-chemical-technolog: BUCT, the Beijing University of Chemical Technology, began in 1958 in the Chaoyang district of the capital. Roughly 12,667 students study here under the Ministry of Education. Its Chinese name means Beijing Chemical Industry University, and it takes part in Project 211, plus the Double First-Class Construction, which suits anyone drawn to chemistry and engineering.
beijing-university-of-chinese-medicine: BUCM, the Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, was established in 1956 and counts among the first higher education institutions in the country devoted to traditional Chinese medicine. The Ministry of Education oversees it, and it takes part in Project 211 together with the Double First-Class Construction.
beijing-university-of-posts-and-telecomm: BUPT, or Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, started in 1955 and now has about 27,000 students. The Education Ministry and the industry and information technology ministry support it jointly. It also joins Project 211, plus the Double First-Class Construction, a good sign for aspiring communications engineers.
beijing-university-of-technology: Beijing University of Technology, founded in 1960, stands in the Chaoyang district of the capital and enrols more than 20,000 students. Its Chinese name means Beijing Industrial University. The city government funds it, and it joins Project 211 as well as the Double First-Class Construction, so expect a solid grounding in industry-minded subjects.
bohai-university: Bohai University stands in Jinzhou, in Liaoning province, and was founded in 2003, which makes it a younger school. This public institution enrols about 23,450 students and belongs to the Province of Liaoning. If you want a large, newer campus in northeastern China, it is worth adding to your shortlist.
capital-medical-university: Capital Medical University, or CCMU, was founded in 1960 and serves the city of Beijing. It belongs to the municipality, with backing shared among the Beijing government, the National Health Commission, plus the education ministry. Those health-sector ties make it an interesting choice for international students planning a medical career.
capital-normal-university: Capital Normal University, or CNU, was established in 1954 and is run by the city of Beijing, with support from the Beijing government and the Ministry of Education. It also forms part of the Double First-Class Construction, and as a normal university it has a tradition in preparing teachers.
capital-university-of-economics-and-busi: CUEB, short for Capital University of Economics and Business, was founded in 1995 in the Fengtai district of Beijing. It has around 20,436 students. The Beijing Municipal People's Government both runs and funds it, so it is a sensible option if you wish to study economics or business in the capital.
central-academy-of-fine-arts: The Central Academy of Fine Arts, known as CAFA, is a public art academy founded in 1918 and run directly by China's Ministry of Education. It is small, with about 4,700 students, and highly selective, turning away more than 90% of applicants each year. A Philippine newspaper has called it China's most prestigious art academy.
central-china-normal-university: Central China Normal University, or CCNU, is a public normal university in Wuhan, Hubei, founded in 1903. About 22,000 students study here. The Education Ministry oversees it, with co-funding from the Hubei provincial government, and it takes part in both Project 211, plus the Double First-Class Construction.
central-conservatory-of-music: The Central Conservatory of Music, or CCOM, is China's national music academy, based in Beijing and founded in 1950. It is a compact community of about 1897 students and answers to the Ministry of Education. Its inclusion in Project 211, plus the Double First-Class Construction makes it a leading destination for serious young musicians.
central-south-university: Central South University, or CSU, calls Changsha, in Hunan, home. It was formed in 2000 by merging three schools: a medical university, a railway university and a technology university. The Ministry of Education oversees it, and it belongs to Project 985, Project 211 and also the Double First-Class Construction. It is ranked #131 by U.S. News and #83 in ARWU.
central-university-of-finance-and-econom: CUFE, a school of finance and economics, is a national public university in Beijing, founded in 1949. It has about 15,117 students. The education and finance ministries, with the Beijing government, sponsor it together, and it takes part in the Double First-Class Construction as well as Project 211, ideal for finance-minded applicants.
changan-university: Chang'an University, called CHD, stands in Xi'an, Shaanxi, was founded in 1951 and serves about 34,000 students. The Ministry of Education oversees it, and several ministries, including Transport and Natural Resources, share the funding with the Shaanxi provincial government. It joins both the Double First-Class Construction, along with Project 211.
changchun-university: Changchun University offers many fields of study in Changchun, in Jilin, and was established in 1946. Its three campuses together cover 1,129,000 square meters. Over the years it has taught upwards of 40,000 undergraduate students, so it brings plenty of experience if you are looking for a broad choice of subjects in northeastern China.
changchun-university-of-chinese-medicine: Changchun University of Chinese Medicine was founded in 1958 as a key university jointly built by Jilin's provincial government and the national traditional Chinese medicine authority. You will find it in Changchun, Jilin's capital in northeast China, which makes it a good base for studying traditional medicine.
changchun-university-of-science-and-tech: This university was founded in 1958 by Wang Daheng, in Changchun, Jilin. It was previously an institute for optics and fine mechanics. Today this public university has around 20,790 students, and its optics heritage makes it an interesting pick for science-minded applicants.
changsha-university-of-science-and-techn: CSUST, the Changsha science and technology university, began in 1956 in Changsha, Hunan. It belongs to Hunan Province, and the provincial government sponsors it together with China's transport ministry, so transport-related fields are a natural strength for students to explore.
chengdu-university-of-technology: The Chengdu University of Technology, or CDUT, is a national public research university in Chengdu, Sichuan, founded in 1956 on the basis of geology faculties from several universities. About 36,000 students study here. It is co-funded by two national ministries and the Sichuan government, and belongs to the Double First-Class Construction Initiative.
chengdu-university-of-traditional-chines: CDUTCM, in Chengdu, Sichuan, is a provincial public medical school founded in 1956. It has about 10,000 students. After the Civil War ended, only four colleges of this kind were set up first, and this was one of them. It also takes part in the Double First-Class Construction.
china-academy-of-art: Set in Hangzhou, in Zhejiang province, the China Academy of Art is a public college devoted to fine arts, opened in 1928. It is run under the provincial government and sits within the Double First-Class Construction. Around 7,234 students study here, so art-minded international applicants will find a focused, creative community to join.
china-agricultural-university: Based in Beijing's Haidian district, China Agricultural University is a public institution that dates back to 1905. It reports to the national Ministry of Education and carries three prestigious labels: Project 211, Project 985, and a place on the Double First-Class list. A well-recognised choice for anyone drawn to agricultural study in the capital.
china-conservatory-of-music: The China Conservatory of Music is a public music school in Beijing's Chaoyang district, founded in 1964. Funded jointly by the city government and the culture and tourism ministry, it concentrates on Chinese ethnic music, covering teaching, research, performance and composition. It also belongs to the Double First-Class Construction, a good sign for aspiring musicians.
china-foreign-affairs-university: If diplomacy and international relations appeal to you, China Foreign Affairs University in Beijing is worth a close look. This public institution, opened in 1955, trains people for foreign service and answers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It is also listed in the Double First-Class Construction programme.
china-pharmaceutical-university: In Nanjing, Jiangsu, China Pharmaceutical University is a public institution with roots in the National College of Pharmacy that go back to 1936. Its current form took shape in 1968 after mergers with other smaller schools. Backed by both the Ministry of Education and Jiangsu province, it carries the Project 211 label and a Double First-Class listing.
china-three-gorges-university: Found in Yichang, Hubei, China Three Gorges University is a provincial public university supported by the Hubei government. It came into being in 2000, when two schools joined forces: Hubei Sanxia College and the Yichang branch of a Wuhan hydraulic and electric power university. With roughly 28,716 students, it offers a lively campus for international learners.
china-university-of-geosciences-beijing: Located in the capital and dating from 1952, the Beijing campus of China University of Geosciences is a national public university. It is overseen by the Ministry of Education and receives joint funding from the Ministry of Natural Resources. Earth-science enthusiasts will note its place in Project 211 and on the Double First-Class list.
china-university-of-geosciences-wuhan: In Wuhan, Hubei, China University of Geosciences is a national public university that first opened in 1952. The Ministry of Education oversees it, with joint support from the Hubei provincial government. It is part of Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction, a solid option if you want to study the earth sciences.
china-university-of-mining-and-technolog: China University of Mining and Technology stands in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, and traces its history to 1909. This public university is overseen by the Ministry of Education, with additional backing from Jiangsu province and the Ministry of Emergency Management. Home to about 35,000 students, it holds Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing.
china-university-of-petroleum-beijing: China University of Petroleum, established in 1953, is a national public institution in Qingdao, Shandong. It reports to the Ministry of Education and is supported by the province of Shandong and five major state energy corporations. Holding Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing, it suits students interested in the energy sector.
china-university-of-petroleum-east-china: Established in 1953, the East China campus of China University of Petroleum sits in Qingdao, Shandong, as a national public institution. The Ministry of Education oversees it, while Shandong province and five major state energy corporations help sponsor it. It also holds Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing, so energy-minded applicants should take note.
china-university-of-political-science-an: Often called Zhengfa University, CUPL began in 1952 and ranks as a national public institution in Beijing. It answers to the Ministry of Education and is co-sponsored by the Beijing municipal government. Law-minded applicants will like its standing in Project 211 and on the Double First-Class list.
china-youth-university-of-political-stud: China Youth University of Political Studies was set up in Beijing during 1985 by the national Communist Youth League, which it remains tied to. The league's First Secretary usually serves as its president. Its 12-hectare campus lies along the West 3rd Ring Northern Road, within easy reach of the capital's city life.
chongqing-jiaotong-university: Chongqing Jiaotong University is a municipal public university in Chongqing's Nan'an district, founded in 1951. Run under the city of Chongqing, it has about 24,000 students. International applicants will find a sizeable campus community in one of China's biggest cities.
chongqing-medical-university: Founded in 1956 in Chongqing, Chongqing Medical University started out as an offshoot of the Shanghai First Medical College, which is now part of Fudan University. The university was formerly called Chongqing University of Medical Sciences. It is a public university with about 25,857 students, suited to those planning a career in medicine.
chongqing-normal-university: Chongqing Normal University is a leading public research university in Chongqing. Its origins lie in East Sichuan Normal School, opened in 1954, and it has since grown into one of the city's top institutions of higher learning. Future teachers and researchers from abroad will find a long tradition of education here.
chongqing-university: Chongqing University is a national public university in Chongqing, founded in 1929 and affiliated with the Ministry of Education. It holds Project 211 and Project 985 status as well as a Double First-Class listing, and its student body numbers around 50,000. A strong pick if you want a large, well-recognised campus in western China.
chongqing-university-of-posts-and-teleco: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications is a municipal public university in the Nan'an district of Chongqing, established in 1950. The city government oversees it. If communications and technology interest you, this university offers a specialised route in a major Chinese city.
communication-university-of-china: Communication University of China is a public university in Beijing's Chaoyang district, founded in 1954 and affiliated with the Ministry of Education. Around 14,623 students study there. It belongs to Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction, making it an appealing option for anyone drawn to media and communication in the capital.
dali-university: Dali University, founded in 1978, is a provincial public institution in the city of Dali in Yunnan, overseen by the Yunnan provincial government. It has roughly 17,900 students. For international applicants who prefer a scenic corner of southwest China to a big-city setting, it is a welcoming place to study.
dalian-jiaotong-university: Dalian Jiaotong University is in Dalian, Liaoning, and is supervised by the provincial government, having earlier been under the Ministry of Railways. Its main campus is close to downtown, with a smaller one in the Hi-tech Zone. Known as Dalian Railway Institute until 2004, it is the only university in Northeast China with a rail transit curriculum.
dalian-maritime-university: Dalian Maritime University, a public institution in Dalian, Liaoning, has a history stretching back to 1909. The Ministry of Transport oversees it, and it holds Project 211 status along with a Double First-Class listing. It is a natural fit if you dream of a career connected with shipping and the sea.
dalian-medical-university: Dalian Medical University is in the coastal city of Dalian, Liaoning, and answers to the provincial government. The university opened its doors in 1947. Prospective international students who want to train in medicine will find an established medical school in a port city.
dalian-university-of-foreign-languages: Dalian University of Foreign Languages, set up in 1964, is a provincial public institution in Dalian, Liaoning. The Liaoning government oversees it, and the student body tops twenty thousand. If languages and cross-cultural study are your passion, this is a friendly place to explore them by the sea.
dalian-university-of-technology: In Dalian's Ganjingzi district, Liaoning, Dalian University of Technology is a public institution established in 1949. The Ministry of Education oversees it, and it holds Project 211 and Project 985 status along with a Double First-Class listing. Engineering and science applicants will find it a well-regarded choice in northeast China.
dongbei-university-of-finance-and-econom: Dongbei University of Finance and Economics, founded in 1952, is a provincial public institution in Dalian, Liaoning. With more than 17,000 students, it counts among the city's longest-running and biggest modern universities. It could suit you well if business, finance or economics is your field.
donghua-university: Donghua University is a public research university in Shanghai, founded in 1951 and affiliated with the Ministry of Education. About 28,497 students are enrolled. It belongs to Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction, offering international applicants a well-connected base in one of China's most cosmopolitan cities.
east-china-normal-university: East China Normal University, opened in 1951, is a public institution in Shanghai. It reports to the Ministry of Education and is co-funded by the Shanghai municipal government. With roughly 32,000 students, it holds Project 211 and Project 985 status plus a Double First-Class listing, a strong option for education-minded applicants.
east-china-university-of-political-scien: Shanghai's ECUPL is a public institution for law and politics, founded in 1952. It has around 15,420 students. International applicants who are curious about legal and political studies can look to this welcoming campus for a specialised education in a major global city.
east-china-university-of-science-and-tec: Shanghai's ECUST was founded in 1952 and reports to the Ministry of Education. It has about 25,000 students and holds Project 211 status along with a Double First-Class listing. Science and engineering fans should find plenty to like at this public university.
fudan-university: Fudan University is a public institution in Shanghai's Yangpu district, founded in 1905. Co-funded by the Shanghai government and linked to the national education ministry, it enrols about 31,900 students. It holds Project 211 and Project 985 status plus a Double First-Class listing, and is among the best-known names for international applicants.
fujian-agriculture-and-forestry-universi: Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University is a provincial public institution in Fuzhou, Fujian, formed in 2000 and focused on agriculture and forestry. It belongs to Fujian province, with joint funding from the provincial government and two national bodies, one for agriculture and rural affairs and one for forestry and grassland.
fujian-medical-university: Fujian Medical University is in Fuzhou, Fujian, and its story begins in 1937 with a provincial medical vocational school. It became a college in 1939 and gained its university name in 1969 after merging with other medical schools, briefly relocating to Quanzhou before returning to Fuzhou in 1978. A fine fit for future doctors.
fujian-normal-university: Fujian Normal University is a public university in Fuzhou, founded in 1907 and often described as Fujian province's cradle of teachers. Around 30,000 students study there. If you hope to become an educator, this long-established campus offers a rich teaching tradition.
fujian-university-of-technology: Fujian University of Technology is a public university in Fuzhou, Fujian, founded in 2002. It is a newer institution that suits international applicants curious about technology-focused study in southeastern China. More details are being gathered, so please confirm programmes directly with the university.
fuzhou-university: Fuzhou University opened in 1958 and is a public university in Fuzhou, the capital of Fujian. The Fujian provincial government oversees it. It is listed under two national programmes, Project 211 and also Double First-Class Construction, which signals its standing among Chinese institutions.
gansu-university-of-chinese-medicine: Based in Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu Province, this public university began in 1978 under the name Gansu College of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is run jointly by the provincial government and the national traditional medicine administration, teaches from bachelor's to doctoral level, and is the only Chinese medicine university in Northwest China allowed to award doctorates.
guangdong-university-of-foreign-studies: Guangdong University of Foreign Studies, often shortened to GDUFS, is a public university in Guangzhou run at provincial level. Its Chinese name translates as Guangdong Foreign Languages and Foreign Trade University, which tells you where its strengths lie, and the current university was formed in 1995.
guangxi-medical-university: Guangxi Medical University sits in Nanning and dates back to 1934, which makes it one of the longest-running medical schools in China. It was named among the country's top twenty universities for medical study in 2010, and its clinical medicine research ranks in the world's top 1% by Essential Science Indicators.
guangxi-minzu-university: Guangxi Minzu University, based in Nanning, is a research-focused provincial institution. It was created in 1952 with a mission to educate the ethnic minority communities of Guangxi, and over the decades it has become best known for ethnology and foreign languages. It makes a fitting choice if those subjects appeal to you.
guangxi-normal-university: Located in Guilin, Guangxi Normal University is a provincial research university that began in 1932 as one of China's earliest teacher training schools. Today it is comprehensive, awarding bachelor's through doctoral degrees, and is known for arts, sciences, teacher education and international exchange. Its campus even contains the Jingjiang Princes' Palace, built in 1372 under the Ming Dynasty.
guangxi-university: Founded in 1928, Guangxi University is a public university in Nanning. It belongs to the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, and both the region and the national education ministry help fund it. It is listed under Project 211 as well as Double First-Class Construction, so it carries national recognition as well as regional roots.
guangxi-university-of-chinese-medicine: Guangxi University of Chinese Medicine is a public university in Nanning, capital of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Established in 1956, it centres on traditional Chinese medicine, combining teaching, research, clinical treatment and drug production, and it is the only standalone Chinese medicine institution among China's five autonomous regions. Around 14,000 students study here.
guangzhou-medical-university: Guangzhou Medical University is a public medical school in Guangzhou, founded in 1958 and funded by the city government. Roughly 10,000 students study on its campuses. The university is included in the national Double First-Class Construction programme, which supports selected institutions in building top-level disciplines.
guangzhou-university-of-chinese-medicine: Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, founded in 1924, is a public university in Guangzhou run by Guangdong Province. As its name suggests, it is devoted to traditional Chinese medicine, and it is part of the national Double First-Class Construction programme for leading universities.
guilin-medical-university: Guilin Medical University is a coeducational public university in Guilin, Guangxi, established in 1935. Its teaching is organised through the School of Medicine, the School of Nursing and Midwifery and a Graduate School, giving students a route into both undergraduate and postgraduate study.
guilin-university-of-electronic-technolo: Guilin University of Electronic Technology, known as GUET, is a public provincial university in Guangxi, southern China. It was founded in 1960, and as the name suggests, its focus is on electronic technology, so it may suit applicants looking at that area.
guizhou-medical-university: Guizhou Medical University, in Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou, is a public university founded in 1938 and home to 19097 students. Subjects include clinical medicine, nursing, pharmacy, preventive medicine and medical laboratory science. The WHO approves it, and Indian students can sit the MCI screening test after finishing the five-year course.
guizhou-minzu-university: Guizhou Minzu University is a provincial public university in Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou province. It was founded in 1951, and it is run at provincial level, so it is a good one to look at if you want to study in Guizhou.
guizhou-normal-university: Guizhou Normal University is a provincial research university in Guiyang, a city once nicknamed the summer capital of China. It was founded in 1941 as one of the first eight teacher training schools in the country, so education is part of its roots.
guizhou-university: Guizhou University was founded in 1902 and stands in the suburbs of Guiyang. This provincial public university is affiliated with Guizhou Province and funded jointly by the provincial government and the Ministry of Education. It appears on two national lists, Project 211 and also Double First-Class Construction.
guizhou-university-of-finance-and-econom: Locals call Guizhou University of Finance and Economics Gui Cai. Founded in 1958 in Guiyang, this provincial research university specialises in management, economics and big data in finance. Students can earn bachelor's, master's or doctoral degrees from 17 departments with 62 undergraduate majors, and the university runs its own institute devoted to big data and finance.
hainan-normal-university: Hainan Normal University has taught students since 1949 in Haikou, the capital of Hainan. It is a public institution managed at provincial level, which makes it a natural option if you want to spend your degree on China's tropical island province.
hainan-university: Hainan University, shortened to HNU or HainanU, was founded in 1958 and teaches about 46,629 students in Haikou. This public university is provincial in character but backed by three funders: Hainan's government plus national ministries for education and for finance. It is listed under Project 211 as well as Double First-Class Construction.
hangzhou-normal-university: Hangzhou Normal University is a public institution in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, that you may also see called Hangzhou Teachers College. It traces its origins to 1908, so more than a hundred years of teaching tradition stand behind the degrees you would study for there.
harbin-engineering-university: Harbin Engineering University, known as HEU, was established in 1953 in Harbin, Heilongjiang, and focuses on engineering, especially shipbuilding, marine technology and nuclear applications. This public research institution reports to the national industry and information technology ministry, and several other bodies including the navy co-fund it. It also takes part in Double First-Class Construction.
harbin-institute-of-technology: Founded in 1920, Harbin Institute of Technology, or HIT, is a science and engineering university in the Nan'gang area of Harbin, Heilongjiang. It enrols about 25,002 students and ranks among China's leading universities. It is listed under Project 211, Project 985 and Double First-Class Construction, and it belongs to the C9 League.
harbin-medical-university: Harbin Medical University, or HMU, is a public university in Harbin in Heilongjiang province. It was founded in 1926, which gives this medical school close to a century of history behind it. It is one to consider if you plan to study medicine in northeast China.
harbin-normal-university: Harbin Normal University, known as HNU, is a university in Harbin, Heilongjiang province, established in 1951. It is a public institution with roughly 32,000 students, so you would join a large and lively community in one of the best-known cities in northern China.
harbin-university-of-science-and-technol: Harbin University of Science and Technology, known as HRBUST, is a coeducational provincial public university in Harbin, Heilongjiang, founded in 1950. It has about 33,496 students and is sponsored by the provincial government together with SASTIND, the national defence science and technology agency.
hebei-medical-university: Hebei Medical University is run by the provincial government and sits in Shijiazhuang, Hebei. Founded in 1894, it is one of the oldest medical institutions in China and holds an AAA grade as a medical school. Around 25,600 students are enrolled, so there is a broad community to join.
hebei-normal-university: Hebei Normal University, a public research university in Shijiazhuang, was founded in 1902 and has more than a century of history. It counts as a provincial key university, and both Hebei Province and the national education department support it financially and otherwise.
hebei-university: Hebei University is a public university in Baoding, Hebei, run at provincial level. It was founded in 1921, so it has a long record of teaching in the province and is worth a look if you want to study in Baoding.
hebei-university-of-economics-and-busine: Hebei University of Economics and Business, or HUEB, was founded in 1953 and is based in Shijiazhuang. It is a public provincial institution with about 21,000 students, affiliated with Hebei and sponsored by its government. Its name signals a focus on economics and business subjects.
hebei-university-of-technology: Hebei University of Technology, or HEBUT, was founded in 1903 and is in Tianjin, even though it belongs to Hebei Province. Its Chinese name means Hebei Industrial University. Hebei and Tianjin governments and the Ministry of Education share funding, about 23,000 students enrol, and it is listed under Project 211 as well as Double First-Class Construction.
hefei-university: Hefei University serves the city of Hefei, capital of Anhui Province. Nuclear chemist Yang Chengzong started it in 1980 as Hefei Union University, and a 2002 merger with two other local schools produced today's university. It teaches 40 bachelor's programs across 16 departments, supports 5 research centers, and has around 17000 students.
hefei-university-of-technology: Hefei University of Technology, or HFUT, was founded in 1945 in Hefei, Anhui, and is a public university with about 25,500 students. The national education ministry oversees it, with extra funding from Anhui's government, the industry and information ministry and SASTIND. Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction both include it.
heilongjiang-university: Heilongjiang University, or HLJU, dates from 1941 and stands in Harbin as a public provincial institution. It is tied to Heilongjiang Province, and three bodies share its sponsorship: the provincial authorities, the Ministry of Education and SASTIND. That mix gives it support from both local and national levels.
heilongjiang-university-of-chinese-medic: Founded in 1959, Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine is a public university for medicine, located in Harbin. Its name tells you the subject: traditional Chinese medicine. It could be a good fit if you want to study that field in the north of China.
henan-university: Henan University, known as HENU, is a provincial public university with a presence in both Zhengzhou and Kaifeng, Henan. It dates from 1912, belongs to Henan Province and is co-funded with the Ministry of Education. It is also included in the Double First-Class Construction programme.
henan-university-of-chinese-medicine: Henan University of Chinese Medicine opened in 1958 and sits in Zhengzhou, Henan, as a public institution. About 19,000 students attend. Its name points to its specialty in traditional Chinese medicine, so it suits applicants aiming for a career in that field.
henan-university-of-technology: Founded in 2004, Henan University of Technology, known as HAUT, is a provincial public institution in Zhengzhou, Henan. Henan Province runs it, with funding shared between the provincial authorities and the National Administration of Grain. It has about 33,500 students, so there is plenty of campus life to join.
hohai-university: Hohai University sits in Nanjing, in Jiangsu Province, and is a public national institution overseen by China's Ministry of Education. Water and ocean authorities share the sponsorship, as do Jiangsu's provincial leaders. Its inclusion in Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes reflects strong national support, and its Nanjing setting is a plus for international students.
huangshan-university: Huangshan University is a higher education institution in the city of Huangshan, in China's Anhui Province. It is run under the authority of the provincial government of Anhui, so it is a good place to look if you are interested in studying in this part of eastern China.
huaqiao-university: Huaqiao University is a public university with campuses in two Fujian cities, Xiamen and Quanzhou. It reports directly to the Chinese Communist Party's United Front Work Department, which gives it a distinctive place among Chinese universities. With around 24,000 students, it offers a sizeable and lively community on China's southeast coast.
huazhong-agricultural-university: Huazhong Agricultural University is based in the urban heart of Wuhan, the capital of Hubei Province in central China. Its roots go back to 1898, when Zhang Zhidong, then governor of Hubei and Hunan, set up the Hubei Farming School under the Qing Dynasty. That long heritage makes it one of the older agricultural schools you can study at in China.
huazhong-university-of-science-and-techn: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, often shortened to HUST, is a public university in the city of Wuhan, Hubei Province. Project 985, Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes all include it, three national schemes that back China's leading research universities. If you are drawn to science and engineering, it deserves a place on your shortlist.
hubei-university-of-chinese-medicine: Hubei University of Chinese Medicine is a provincial public university in Wuhan, Hubei Province. It was previously called Hubei Traditional Chinese Medicine College. As the name suggests, it focuses on traditional Chinese medicine, which makes it a natural fit if you hope to study that field in China.
hunan-normal-university: Hunan Normal University is a public university run at provincial level in Changsha, the capital of Hunan Province. The Hunan government and China's education ministry fund it jointly. It takes part in Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes, two national initiatives that recognise strong universities. It is a fine option if teacher education and the wider humanities and sciences appeal to you.
hunan-university: Hunan University is a national public university in the Yuelu district of Changsha, Hunan Province, funded by China's Ministry of Education. Its national recognition includes Project 211, Project 985 and Double First-Class programmes, and it also belongs to the BRICS Universities League. That makes it a well-connected choice for international students.
inner-mongolia-agricultural-university: Inner Mongolia Agricultural University was established in 1952 and is based in Hohhot, the capital of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. It comes under the regional government and offers more than 100 undergraduate programmes alongside postgraduate courses. Subjects span agriculture, engineering, science, art, business and management, so you will find plenty of directions to explore.
inner-mongolia-normal-university: Inner Mongolia Normal University is a public university in Hohhot, the capital of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in northern China. It is managed by the regional government, and its name points to a strong tradition in teacher education. It could suit you if you want to experience study life in this region.
inner-mongolia-university: Inner Mongolia University is a public university at provincial level in Hohhot, the capital of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. The regional government and China's Ministry of Education support it together, and it takes part in Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes. With about 23,203 students, it has a substantial campus community for you to join.
inner-mongolia-university-of-technology: Inner Mongolia University of Technology began in 1951 as the Suiyuan Higher Technical School, became a polytechnic institute after 1958, and took its present name in 1993. It runs three campuses, two in Hohhot and one in the city of Ordos. The regional government oversees it, and it is a solid technical choice with around 27,000 students.
jiamusi-university: Jiamusi University is a public university in Jiamusi, in the far northeast of Heilongjiang Province, and it answers to the provincial government. Thanks to its eastern location, it is said to be the first university in China to see the sun rise each morning, which is a charming detail for anyone considering a study year there.
jiangnan-university: Jiangnan University is a public university in Wuxi, Jiangsu Province. The Ministry of Education oversees it, together with the Jiangsu provincial government. Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes both include it, two national schemes for strong universities. Wuxi lies in one of China's most developed regions, which makes this a convenient base for international students.
jiangsu-normal-university: Jiangsu Normal University is a provincial key public university in Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province. China's Ministry of Education and the Jiangsu government built it up together. It is home to roughly 25,000 students, so you would join a busy campus, and it makes a good option if you are interested in teacher training and related fields.
jiangsu-university: Jiangsu University is a public university at provincial level in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu. It is affiliated with the provincial government and also receives backing from education and agriculture ministries at national level. With around 34,100 students, it is a large and active campus that welcomes learners from many backgrounds.
jiangxi-agricultural-university: Jiangxi Agricultural University lies in the northern suburbs of Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province. It is a key university run by the province and was among the first in China to award bachelor's and master's degrees. Around 26,000 students study here, so it offers a sizeable community with a strong agricultural focus.
jiangxi-normal-university: Jiangxi Normal University is in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province, and is jointly sponsored by China's education ministry and the provincial government. Its degrees cover literature, history, philosophy, economics, management, law, sciences, engineering, education and the arts, and it has about 30,692 students. It also plays an influential part in the province's social and cultural life.
jiangxi-university-of-chinese-medicine: Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine is a medical university in Nanchang, Jiangxi Province. The provincial government leads it, and its focus is on traditional Chinese medicine. If you want to explore this tradition in the place where it is taught, it could be a rewarding choice.
jiangxi-university-of-finance-and-econom: Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics is a public, coeducational research university in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province. As the name suggests, it focuses on finance and economics. About 30,000 students attend, giving international applicants a large and lively community in which to study business-related subjects.
jilin-agricultural-university: Jilin Agricultural University is a public agricultural university in Changchun, Jilin Province, founded in 1948. It is linked to the Jilin provincial government and to China's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, and it has a place in the national programme supporting western and central China. Around 18,000 students study here.
jilin-normal-university: Jilin Normal University is in Siping, in northeast China's Jilin Province, and was once known as the Siping Normal Institute. It was founded in 1958 and serves as a training centre for teachers across the province. Seminars and classes there have recently helped prepare over 22,000 teachers.
jilin-university: Jilin University is a public university in Changchun, the capital of Jilin Province, and it is overseen by China's Ministry of Education. Project 211, Project 985 and Double First-Class programmes all include it, which together mark it out as one of the country's leading universities and a strong choice for international study.
jinan-university: Jinan University, in the city of Guangzhou in Guangdong Province, is a national public institution. It is managed jointly by the Party's United Front Work Department, China's education ministry and the Guangdong provincial government. It takes part in Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes, and ranks among 13 high-level Guangdong universities. Roughly 50,535 students study there.
jingdezhen-ceramic-university: Jingdezhen Ceramic University stands in the Jiangxi city of Jingdezhen and is the only higher education institution in China dedicated to ceramic arts. The area has long been central to Chinese ceramics, so students link modern teaching with ancient craft. Around 15,000 students attend, and one well-known alumnus is the artist Jackson Li.
jinzhou-medical-university: Jinzhou Medical University is a university in the city of Jinzhou, in Liaoning Province, northeast China. As its name makes clear, it is a medical institution, so it is worth a look if you hope to study medicine or health sciences in this part of the country.
kunming-medical-university: Kunming Medical University, which used to be named Kunming Medical College, trains doctors in Kunming, in China's Yunnan Province. If you are planning a career in medicine, it offers a chance to study in the southwest of the country, in a city known as the provincial capital.
kunming-university-of-science-and-techno: Kunming University of Science and Technology, known as KUST, is in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan Province in southwestern China. It focuses on science and technology, so it is a natural fit for students who want to study technical subjects while living in this southwestern provincial capital.
lanzhou-jiaotong-university: Lanzhou Jiaotong University is a transport-focused university in Lanzhou, in China's Gansu Province. If you are interested in railways, transport and related engineering, this is a specialist place to study, set in a northwestern city quite different from the big coastal centres.
lanzhou-university: Lanzhou University is a public university in the Gansu capital of Lanzhou, run under China's Ministry of Education. Project 211, Project 985 and Double First-Class programmes all include it, recognising the country's leading institutions. For international students, it offers a chance to study in China's northwest at a nationally supported university.
lanzhou-university-of-technology: Lanzhou University of Technology is a science and technology university in Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu Province. It is a public institution, and engineering and technical subjects are its core strength. It could suit you well if you are looking for a practical technical education in northwest China.
liaoning-normal-university: Liaoning Normal University is a comprehensive university in Dalian, Liaoning Province, with a particular emphasis on teacher training. Its teacher college is the largest in the province. About 13,166 students study here, and Dalian's coastal setting makes it an appealing choice for future educators from abroad.
liaoning-petrochemical-university: Liaoning Petrochemical University is in Fushun, Liaoning Province, in northeast China, and it is administered by the provincial government. Its name reflects a focus on petroleum and chemical fields, and it has around 15,000 students. It could be a fitting choice if those industries interest you.
liaoning-technical-university: Liaoning Technical University, also known as Liaoning University of Engineering and Technology, has three campuses. Two are in Fuxin and one is in Huludao, all in Liaoning Province. The provincial government and the State Administration of Work Safety run it together. With about 25,000 students, it is a good fit for engineering-minded applicants.
liaoning-university: Liaoning University is a public university in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, established in 1948. The provincial government and the Ministry of Education fund it together, and it takes part in Project 211 and Double First-Class programmes. About 17,000 students study here, so you would find a friendly, mid-sized campus in a major northeastern city.
liaoning-university-of-technology: Liaoning University of Technology, which used to be the Liaoning Institute of Technology, can be found in Jinzhou, in northeast China's Liaoning Province. Around 14,578 students study here. With its technical focus, it is a practical option for international students who want to learn engineering-related subjects in northeast China.
liaoning-university-of-traditional-chine: If traditional Chinese medicine is the field you want to study, Liaoning University of Traditional Chinese Medicine (LNUTCM) is worth a look. It sits in Liaoning Province, with its main campus in Shenyang's Huanggu District, a second campus in Dalian, and another in Benxi, so you can ask which site hosts your program.
ludong-university: Ludong University is a provincial public university in the coastal city of Yantai, Shandong. It began in 1958 as a teachers' school, became a normal college in 1984, and earned full university status in 2006. Today it teaches 48 majors across the arts and sciences, giving newcomers a broad choice of subjects.
minzu-university-of-china: Minzu University of China stands in Beijing as a national public institution. It opened in 1941 and today enrolls roughly 15,800 students. The National Ethnic Affairs Commission is its parent body, and its place in Project 985, Project 211 and the Double First-Class scheme shows how highly the state values it.
nanchang-hangkong-university: Nanchang Hangkong University, also called Nanchang Aeronautics University, is a public school in Nanchang, the city where China built its first aircraft. Opened in 1952, it began as an engineering college and has grown into a multidisciplinary campus of about 19,000 students, with a special strength in aeronautics and defense technology. Jiangxi's provincial government and an industry ministry jointly supervise it.
nanchang-university: Founded in 1921, Nanchang University is a public research university in the city of Nanchang, Jiangxi. Both the provincial government and the national Ministry of Education sponsor it. With Project 211 recognition and a place on the Double First-Class list, it is a well-funded, research-minded campus for international students to consider.
nanjing-agricultural-university: Nanjing Agricultural University has taught since 1902, and about 17,000 students now study at this public campus in Nanjing, Jiangsu. National and provincial governments share its sponsorship, and it holds Project 211 status alongside a place on the Double First-Class list. Consider it if agriculture and the life sciences are your goal.
nanjing-forestry-university: Nanjing Forestry University, dating back to 1902, sits in Nanjing, Jiangsu, as a public university under provincial care. Its roughly 30,000 students make for a lively, fairly large campus. It also appears on China's Double First-Class list, the national drive to build up leading universities and disciplines.
nanjing-medical-university: Medical students have trained at Nanjing Medical University since 1934. This public university in Nanjing, Jiangsu, answers to the provincial government and appears on the Double First-Class list. If you hope to study medicine in China, its focus on health and medical education makes it a natural place to start your search.
nanjing-normal-university: With roots reaching back to 1902, Nanjing Normal University serves roughly 30,933 students in Nanjing, Jiangsu. Provincial authorities and the Ministry of Education support this public institution together. Its Project 211 status and its Double First-Class listing give it a respected place among China's teaching-oriented universities.
nanjing-university: Founded in 1902, Nanjing University teaches about 13,934 students and has campuses in both Nanjing and Suzhou, Jiangsu. The Ministry of Education sponsors it. Holding Project 985 and Project 211 status, a Double First-Class place, and membership of the elite C9 League, it ranks among China's best-known public universities.
nanjing-university-of-aeronautics-and-as: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, or NUAA, was founded in 1952 and now has about 19,899 students on its public campus in Nanjing, Jiangsu. The national ministry responsible for industry and information technology oversees it. It counts among the Seven Sons of National Defence and holds Project 211 status, a good fit for future engineers.
nanjing-university-of-chinese-medicine: Founded in 1954, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine serves students in Nanjing, Jiangsu, as a public university under provincial supervision. It takes part in the Double First-Class scheme. Prospective international students who want to learn traditional Chinese medicine in a university setting will find it a focused, specialist choice.
nanjing-university-of-information-scienc: NUIST was founded in 1960 and takes its name from information science and technology. This public university in Nanjing, Jiangsu, operates under the provincial government and is included in the Double First-Class scheme. It is worth checking out if studying information science or technology appeals to you.
nanjing-university-of-posts-and-telecomm: NJUPT has a history that goes back to 1942 and carries posts and telecommunications in its full name. Based in Nanjing, Jiangsu, this public university answers to the provincial government and is included in the Double First-Class scheme. Students curious about communications and telecom may find its name a helpful hint.
nanjing-university-of-science-and-techno: Teaching since 1953, NJUST (Nanjing University of Science and Technology) stands in Xuanwu, Nanjing, and has about 27,063 students. This public institution answers to the national ministry for industry and information technology, and is co-sponsored by the Ministry of Education and Jiangsu's government. It also holds Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing.
nanjing-university-of-the-arts: Also called the Nanjing Arts Institute, Nanjing University of the Arts offers undergraduate and graduate degrees. Its programs center on fine arts, design and related subjects, so it suits international applicants who want to develop their artistic and design skills in a dedicated arts setting.
nankai-university: Nankai University, founded in 1919, is a national public research university in Tianjin with about 17,339 students. The Ministry of Education oversees it. With Project 985 and Project 211 recognition and a Double First-Class listing, it ranks among China's most strongly supported universities and is an attractive choice for ambitious international applicants.
nantong-university: Nantong University, in Nantong, Jiangsu, traces its history to 1912 and teaches about 30,000 students. Provincial authorities run this public institution, and it also receives funding from the Ministry of Transport together with the Jiangsu people's government, giving it a mix of local and national support.
ningbo-university: Ningbo University opened in 1986 in the Jiangbei area of Ningbo, Zhejiang, and enrolls about 25,000 students. The Ningbo Municipal People's Government oversees this city-run public university. Being part of the Double First-Class scheme, it offers international students a modern, city-backed campus in one of Zhejiang's major cities.
ningbo-university-of-technology: Ningbo University of Technology is a comprehensive provincial university in Ningbo, in China's Zhejiang province. It was founded in 1983 and is a public institution, so it can suit students who want a broad range of subjects, not just a single specialty, in a lively coastal city setting.
ningxia-medical-university: Ningxia Medical University, once called Ningxia Medical College, is a public medical school in Yinchuan, the capital city of Ningxia. It was founded in 1958 and concentrates on medical education, making it a relevant destination for international students who hope to study medicine or health sciences in northwest China.
ningxia-university: Ningxia University, founded in 1958, serves about 28610 students in Yinchuan as a regional public institution. The Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region and the Ministry of Education fund it jointly. Its Project 211 status and Double First-Class listing mark it as a solid, well-supported campus in northwest China.
north-china-electric-power-university: Established in 1958 to serve the energy sector, North China Electric Power University is a public institution in Beijing. National education authorities, the China Electricity Council and a body made up of 12 large state-owned power corporations back it together. With Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing, it is a strong pick for energy-minded students.
north-china-university-of-technology: North China University of Technology, founded in 1947, sits in Beijing's Shijingshan district and teaches about 16000 students. It is a public university funded by the Beijing city government. International students who prefer a city-run technical university in the capital, rather than a national flagship, may find it a friendly, practical option.
northeast-agricultural-university: Founded in 1948, Northeast Agricultural University in Harbin, Heilongjiang, is regarded as one of China's key agricultural universities. The Heilongjiang provincial government and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs oversee it. It holds Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing, so it is a great choice for agricultural study.
northeast-electric-power-university: Northeast Electric Power University opened in 1949 in Jilin City, in Jilin province. Around 14,373 students attend this public university, which the Jilin provincial government sponsors. As the name suggests, it focuses on electric power, so it could appeal to students interested in energy and related engineering fields.
northeast-forestry-university: Northeast Forestry University was established in 1952 in Harbin, Heilongjiang, and has around 28,000 students. National education authorities, the national forestry and grassland body and the provincial government built it together. Holding Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing, it is a leading name for forestry-related study.
northeast-normal-university: Northeast Normal University, founded in 1946, trains teachers and scholars in Changchun, Jilin, and has about 15,191 students. The national Ministry of Education and the provincial government fund it jointly. Its Project 211 status and Double First-Class listing make it a respected destination for anyone drawn to teacher education and the humanities.
northeastern-university: Northeastern University, called Dongbei Daxue in Chinese, was founded in 1923 and stands in Shenyang, capital of Liaoning Province. It belongs to the national group run under the Ministry of Education, with shared support from SASTIND and the Liaoning and Shenyang governments, which helps place it among the country's best-supported universities.
northwest-af-university: Northwest A&F University was founded in 1934 in Yangling District, Xianyang, Shaanxi, and has about 28,964 students. Its full name points to agriculture and forestry science and technology. The Ministry of Education oversees this national public university, which holds Project 985 and Project 211 status plus a Double First-Class listing.
northwest-normal-university: In Lanzhou, Gansu Province, Northwest Normal University is a public institution that the State Council has authorized to award associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees across more than 80 subject areas, so international students can find many study levels and fields on its campus in northwest China.
northwestern-polytechnical-university: Northwestern Polytechnical University, or NWPU, was founded in 1938 and has about 28,131 students in Xi'an, Shaanxi. This public school focuses on science and engineering and answers to the national ministry for industry and information technology. It holds Project 985 and Project 211 status plus a Double First-Class listing, a strong pick for future engineers.
ocean-university-of-china: Established in 1924, Ocean University of China stands in the coastal city of Qingdao, Shandong, under the Ministry of Education. It holds Project 985 and Project 211 status and a Double First-Class listing. Its name signals a strong connection to marine and ocean studies, which suits students drawn to the sea.
peking-university: Peking University, or PKU, was founded in 1898 in Beijing's Haidian district and has about 49,821 students. The Ministry of Education both oversees and funds it. With Project 985 and Project 211 status, a Double First-Class listing and membership of the C9 League of leading research universities, it is among China's most famous campuses.
qingdao-university: Qingdao University is a key provincial research university in the coastal city of Qingdao, Shandong. Founded in 1985, it is a public university with about 46,000 students, which makes it a big and busy campus. It also runs a medical school, so health-minded international students may want to explore it.
qingdao-university-of-science-and-techno: Founded in 1950, QUST started out as a chemical-industry college. Today this public university in Qingdao has widened into a comprehensive, multidisciplinary school, with degrees spanning many areas such as science, technology, business, medicine, law and the arts, so there is plenty of variety for international students.
qinghai-minzu-university: Qinghai Minzu University calls Xining, the capital of Qinghai Province, home. Opened in December 1949, it holds the distinction of being the earliest university of higher education in the whole province, so it carries a long local tradition. Its name in Chinese is 青海民族大学, which is handy to know when you search for application details.
qinghai-university: Qinghai University sits in Xining, Qinghai, and has been a public institution since 1958, with roughly 27,000 students today. The provincial government and the Ministry of Education support it together. It is also listed under the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211, two national programmes that single out leading Chinese universities.
qiqihar-university: Qiqihar University sits in Qiqihar City, in the western part of Heilongjiang in northeastern China. This public university was founded in 1953 and has around 29,000 students. It is run under the Heilongjiang provincial government, which also funds it, so expect a regional campus feel with a large student community.
renmin-university-of-china: Renmin University of China, often shortened to RUC, lies in Beijing's Haidian district and has roots going back to 1937. Funding comes jointly from both the Education Ministry and Beijing's city government. Its inclusion in Project 985, Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction marks it as a nationally prominent public university.
shaanxi-normal-university: Shaanxi Normal University, known as SNNU, stands in Chang'an District, Xi'an, and has been open since 1944. It reports to the Ministry of Education and counts about 17,502 students. Being part of Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction puts it among nationally recognised public universities that welcome study plans from abroad.
shaanxi-university-of-chinese-medicine: Based in Xianyang, Shaanxi Province, this public medical university dates from 1952 and focuses on traditional Chinese medicine. If you want to study that field in a smaller, specialist setting in western China, Shaanxi University of Chinese Medicine is worth adding to your shortlist.
shandong-normal-university: Shandong Normal University is a public university in Jinan, the capital of Shandong Province. Its beginnings go back to 1950, which makes it one of the first institutions of higher learning set up in the province after the People's Republic was founded. Students who want to train in teaching and related subjects in eastern China may find it a natural fit.
shandong-university: Shandong University, or SDU, is based in Jinan, Shandong, and traces its origins all the way back to 1733. This public institution answers to the Ministry of Education and takes part in Project 985, Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction. For international applicants, that long history and national standing make it a strong choice.
shandong-university-of-science-and-techn: Shandong University of Science and Technology, or SDUST, is a provincial public university in the coastal city of Qingdao. Established in 1951, it is run and funded by the Shandong provincial government. As the name hints, its courses lean toward science and technology, making it a practical option if you are planning a technical degree.
shandong-university-of-technology: Shandong University of Technology, or SDUT, is a public university in Zibo, Shandong. Set up in 1956, it concentrates on engineering sciences and is home to around 39,300 students. If you are hoping to study engineering in a large, busy campus community in eastern China, this university deserves a close look.
shanghai-conservatory-of-music: Founded on 27 November 1927, the Shanghai Conservatory of Music is a public college run by the municipal government of Shanghai. It also takes part in the Double First-Class Construction programme. Aspiring musicians from overseas can find a long-established home for serious musical training here.
shanghai-international-studies-universit: Shanghai International Studies University, called SHISU for short, began in 1949 and is a public institution in Shanghai. Funding is shared between the Education Ministry and Shanghai's city government. Placement in the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211 shows it is well recognised across China, and international students are a natural part of its community.
shanghai-jiao-tong-university: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, or SJTU, is one of Shanghai's best-known public institutions, with a history stretching back to 1896. It belongs to the Ministry of Education, features in Project 985, Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction, and sits in the C9 League of leading Chinese universities. It lists around 16,221 students.
shanghai-maritime-university: Shanghai Maritime University, or SHMTU, has roots going back to 1909 and operates as a public university under municipal control in Shanghai. The city government runs it together with the Ministry of Transportation. Its sea and shipping focus, together with a very large student body, makes it a lively place to study.
shanghai-normal-university: Shanghai Normal University, or SHNU, was founded in 1954 and is a public research university home to about 21,256 students. It ranks as one of the city's three key universities, alongside Shanghai University and the science and technology university of the same city, all strongly backed by Shanghai's municipal government.
shanghai-ocean-university: Shanghai Ocean University, or SHOU, goes back to 1912 and is a public research university devoted to aquaculture, marine science and engineering. It belongs to the Double First-Class Initiative. Backing comes from the Ministry of Natural Resources, the Shanghai government and the agriculture and rural affairs ministry.
shanghai-university: Shanghai University, known as SHU, was founded in 1994 and is owned by the Shanghai city government. This municipal public institution belongs to the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211. With about 56,753 students, it makes a big and lively campus for international students who want to study in the city.
shanghai-university-of-finance-and-econo: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, or SUFE, began in 1917 and is a public institution in Shanghai. The Ministry of Education oversees it, and it takes part in Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction. Roughly 12,666 students attend, and it suits anyone who wants to study finance or economics in China's financial hub.
shanghai-university-of-international-bus: SUIBE, a Shanghai school for international business and economics, was founded in 1960. It is a public university tied to Shanghai and paid for by its municipal government. With around 14,000 students, it is a comfortably sized campus for those interested in business and economics.
shanghai-university-of-political-science: Despite the word university in its English name, this Shanghai institution, which focuses on political science and law, is a public college run by the city and has not yet been granted full university status. Keep that in mind when comparing options, and check its current programmes directly before applying.
shanghai-university-of-sport: Founded in 1952 in Shanghai's Yangpu district, the Shanghai University of Sport, or SUS, is a public university overseen by the city. It also forms part of the Double First-Class Construction. If sport science or physical education is your passion, it offers a specialist setting in one of China's biggest cities.
shanghai-university-of-traditional-chine: This Shanghai medical institution, sometimes called Shanghai University of Chinese Medicine, can trace its history to 1916 and counts among the four earliest Chinese medicine colleges in the country. In 2026 it came second in the city's own ranking for universities in this field. It is a leading choice for traditional medicine.
shantou-university: Shantou University, or STU, sits in Shantou, Guangdong, and was founded in 1981 with approval from the State Council. It falls under the provincial Project 211 programme and has roughly 10,294 students. If you like the idea of studying in a coastal city in eastern Guangdong, it is worth a closer look.
shantou-university-medical-college: Shantou University Medical College, or SUMC, serves as the medical school for Shantou University in eastern Guangdong. Its history goes back to 1924. Today it is a public school with more than ten affiliated and teaching hospitals, so medical teaching, research and patient care all happen close together.
shanxi-university: Shanxi University, or SXU, was founded in 1902 and stands in Taiyuan, Shanxi, as a public university run at provincial level. It also forms part of the Double First-Class Construction. Around 31,528 students study there, so international students join a large and well-established community in northern China.
shanxi-university-of-chinese-medicine: Founded in 1978, this public medical university in Taiyuan, Shanxi Province, concentrates on traditional Chinese medicine. Shanxi University of Chinese Medicine may suit you if you want to study this discipline at a specialist institution in northern China.
shenyang-aerospace-university: Shenyang Aerospace University, or SAU, is in Shenyang, Liaoning, in northeast China. Founded in 1952 as a public institution, it was formerly called Shenyang Institute of Aeronautical Engineering. It trains students for both military and civil aviation industries, and enrols about 7000, so aviation-minded applicants will feel at home.
shenyang-jianzhu-university: Shenyang Jianzhu University, written 沈阳建筑大学 in Chinese, is located in Shenyang, Liaoning, and its history begins in 1948. The provincial government oversees the university. Its name points to a focus on architecture and construction, though you should confirm current programme details with the admissions office before applying.
shenyang-ligong-university: Shenyang Ligong University, or SYLU, traces back to 1948 and operates under the provincial government in Shenyang, Liaoning. It has about 28,000 students. Its campus is located in the newer Hunnan New District, so expect a modern setting on the edge of the city.
shenyang-normal-university: Shenyang Normal University, or SYNU, is a broad-based public university in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, founded in 1951. It is overseen by the provincial government and has about 23,037 students. With its wide range of subjects, it can suit international students who are still deciding on a field.
shenyang-university-of-technology: Shenyang University of Technology, or SUT, began in 1949 and operates under the provincial government in Shenyang, Liaoning. Its Chinese name is 沈阳工业大学, and the word technology in its title suggests a technical emphasis, though it is wise to check current programmes before you apply.
shihezi-university: Shihezi University, or SHZU, was founded in 1996 in Shihezi, Xinjiang. This public institution belongs to the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps (the Corps), and both the Corps and the Ministry of Education provide funding. It is also included in the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211, giving it national standing in China's far west.
sichuan-agricultural-university: Sichuan Agricultural University, or SCAU, has origins in 1906 and has its headquarters in Ya'an, Sichuan. The Ministry of Education and the Sichuan government co-sponsor this provincial agricultural institution. Being in the Double First-Class Construction and Project 211 means farming-related study here carries national weight.
sichuan-international-studies-university: Sichuan International Studies University, or SISU, despite its name, is located in Chongqing. Founded in 1950 as a public research university, it ranks among the first four higher education institutions in China to specialise in foreign languages. It enrols around 8,000 students, making it a focused option for language lovers.
sichuan-university: Sichuan University, or SCU, in Chengdu, Sichuan, was founded in 1896 and has a very large student body, well above the typical campus. The Ministry of Education both oversees and funds this public university, which features in Project 985, Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction. It is a major name in western China.
south-china-agricultural-university: South China Agricultural University, or SCAU, started in 1909 in Guangzhou, Guangdong, and is a public institution run at provincial level. It is affiliated with the Guangdong government and also belongs to the Double First-Class Construction. Its agricultural focus makes it a sound choice for farming, food and plant studies in southern China.
south-china-normal-university: South China Normal University, often shortened to SCNU, is a public teacher-training university based in Guangzhou, Guangdong. Opened in 1933, it is run by the provincial government together with the Ministry of Education, and it belongs to both Project 211 and the Double First-Class Construction programme.
south-china-university-of-technology: SCUT, short for South China University of Technology, is a coeducational public university in Guangzhou, Guangdong, with roots going back to 1918. It is overseen by the Ministry of Education and the Guangdong provincial government, and it holds Project 211 and Project 985 status and is in the Double First-Class Construction plan.
southeast-university: Known as SEU, this Nanjing institution in Jiangsu was first established in 1921 and is publicly run. About 16,125 students study there, and it answers to China's Ministry of Education. Applicants should know it holds Project 211 and Project 985 status and is in the Double First-Class Construction initiative.
southern-medical-university: Southern Medical University is a public medical school in Baiyun district, Guangzhou, started in 1951. It used to be a military-run institution, but in 2004 control passed completely to the Guangdong provincial government, and today it operates as a provincial public university.
southern-university-of-science-and-techn: SUSTech is a young public university in Shenzhen, Guangdong, set up in 2010 and funded by the city government. More than 10,000 students were enrolled in 2022. It has also been placed in the Double First-Class Construction programme, which suits applicants wanting a newer campus.
southwest-jiaotong-university: Southwest Jiaotong University (SWJTU) is a public science and engineering research university in Chengdu, Sichuan, whose story starts in 1896. Around 43,503 students attend. Several backers support it, among them China Railway Corporation, the education ministry and local governments, and it has Project 211 status and is in the Double First-Class Construction plan.
southwest-medical-university: Southwest Medical University is a public medical school located in Luzhou, Sichuan, which began teaching in 1951. Before taking its present name, it was called Luzhou Medical College. Its abbreviation is SWMU, and it is a sensible option for those hoping to study medicine in western China.
southwest-petroleum-university: Southwest Petroleum University (SWPU), founded in 1958, is a public university run by Sichuan province in Chengdu and home to around 32,498 students.
